questions.q: Which four pillars open the summary's list of caste's foundations?
a: Divine will, heritability, endogamy, and purity
Hierarchy, dehumanization, terror, and superiority
Wealth, education, land, and title
Religion, language, region, and ancestry
questions.why: Lesson 1 covers divine will, being born into a caste, marriage within it and fears about purity.

questions.q: What does heritability mean as a pillar of caste?
a: You are born into your parents' caste
You can earn a higher caste through work
You choose your caste when you marry
Your caste depends on where you live
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines heritability simply: a person inherits the caste of their parents at birth.

questions.q: What role does terror play in upholding a caste system?
a: It enforces control through whippings, burnings, and hangings
It keeps members loyal through shared rituals
It shields lower castes from outside threats
It offers lower castes a route upward
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists terror as enforcement and cruelty as control, citing violence on plantations and after slavery.

questions.q: What does the purity versus pollution pillar justify?
a: Keeping bloodlines separate from other groups
Sharing water and pools equally
Allowing marriage across castes
Giving lower castes better housing
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites bans on Jewish people touching Aryan water and on African-Americans using swimming pools.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest as a first step toward dismantling caste?
a: Make people aware that it exists
Remove every Confederate statue at once
Pass a single federal law
Wait for attitudes to shift on their own
questions.why: Lesson 3 says awareness comes first, followed by supporting those trying to break free of a lower caste.
